name: MN-07
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+18 partisan lean makes this among the most Republican seats in Minnesota
Fischbach holds a commanding fundraising lead ($1.29M raised, $920K on hand vs. $335K and $114K for Osberg)
Prediction markets price the Republican at about 96%
No public polls or expert ratings exist, leaving fundamentals as the main guide
model.rationale: The R+18 district, Fischbach's large financial advantage, and market pricing near 96% Republican all point to a comfortable incumbent win, with no contrary evidence on record to justify moving away from that picture.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Fischbach or an unexpected campaign-level shock would be the most plausible route to tightening this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
MN-07 is one of the most Republican-leaning districts in Minnesota, with a partisan lean of roughly R+18. Michelle Fischbach, the incumbent, is running for re-election after securing renomination, and prediction markets give her about a 96% chance of victory. No public polls or expert race ratings are available for this contest, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, fundraising, and market pricing.

Fischbach holds a clear financial edge, having raised about $1.29 million to challenger Erik Osberg's $335,000, and she enters the general election with nearly $920,000 on hand. A Republican-leaning national environment adds to her advantage. Osberg faces an uphill battle in a district that has consistently backed Republicans by wide margins, and the race rates as Safe Republican.
